action: Plan to patch PHP on Thursday 19 November as soon as the release lands (14:00-14:30 UTC per the PHP Foundation notice cited by The Register). Inventory PHP versions on internet-facing servers, and check for the non-default configurations the advisory describes.
exec: PHP runs on most web servers with a known server-side language; a critical release is pre-announced for Thursday, so teams can schedule patching now. Earlier PHP2Shell flaws are already exploited.
plain: The PHP project says it will release a critical security update on Thursday, so server owners can get ready to patch quickly.

key_findings: A critical PHP security release is planned for Thursday 14:00-14:30 UTC; the highest-severity bugs are rated critical.
The Register says CVE-2026-115560 is an RCE bug needing a non-default or uncommon setup, with a configuration setting that mitigates it.
heise reports all supported PHP versions are affected and that some issues are critical only in unusual setups.
recommendations: Prepare to patch on release day.

summary: The PHP project has announced a critical security release for Thursday, November 19, after several issues rated critical in non-default or unusual setups. The Register names CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution bug with a configuration mitigation. heise says all supported PHP versions are affected. Patches are not yet released. Earlier PHP2Shell flaws are already exploited.
title: PHP Foundation pre-announces a critical security release for Thursday

validation.note: The Register and heise both report the planned release; the php.net notices they cite were not opened. No fixed versions are published yet.

review.note: Compared with The Register and heise: release on Thursday Nov 19, critical issues in non-default setups, all supported versions, CVE-2026-115560 RCE with config mitigation, PHP2Shell exploited.
